# TEST262 — the JavaScript grammar against test262 (auto-generated)

<!-- AUTO-GENERATED by `node test/test262.ts --write`. Do not edit by hand. -->

test262 is the ECMAScript conformance suite, and JavaScript's oracle here ([ROADMAP](ROADMAP.md) item 6;
`tsc` remains the oracle for TypeScript-only syntax, [CORRECTNESS.md](CORRECTNESS.md)). Every test under
`test/language/` and `test/annexB/language/` is parsed by the interpreter over `javascript.ts`, and its
verdict compared with the one the test's front matter states: a test whose `negative.phase` is `parse`
must not parse; every other test must (a resolution or runtime error still parses). The sources are read
from a checkout, never run, never copied into this repository. The harness and its rules:
[`test/test262.ts`](../test/test262.ts); the classes: [`test/test262-classes.ts`](../test/test262-classes.ts);
every disagreeing file: [`test/test262-record.txt`](../test/test262-record.txt). The gate `conformance/test262`
fails when either is stale; `node test/test262.ts --write` re-records.

Corpus: `tc39/test262@ebf6ae620a0f292b4845cd4099cb9096735e64ae` (pin: `test/test262.sha`) · 24677 tests (4477 parse-negative) · 283 `_FIXTURE.js` modules skipped (imported by tests, not tests).

Goal and mode: `javascript.ts` has one entry, `Program`, and no script / module goal or strict mode switch
(the [Await] / [Yield] contexts are its only parameters). So it gives every run of a test the same verdict:
a test that test262 runs both sloppy and strict, or only in one mode, or as a module, is parsed once (the
first run's text: `"use strict";` prepended for `onlyStrict`). What depends on the goal or the mode is a class
of its own below (`needs-parameter`).

**21296 of 24677 agree (86.3%).**

## Classes

Every disagreement has one cause class, the first whose predicate holds (the order of
`test/test262-classes.ts`); each class was read on a sample of its files. Verdicts: **grammar bug** (no goal
or mode derives it, or derivable syntax refused); **adding** (valid syntax the grammar lacks, decided to add);
**needs-parameter** (the script / module goal, strict mode, [Return] or another parameterised production the
engine lacks: roadmap item 4); **early error** (a static-semantic rule: not the context-free grammar's,
[CORRECTNESS.md](CORRECTNESS.md), but a checker's over the tree, which is not built; see "Early errors" below).
"acorn agrees": acorn, a production parser that implements most early errors, gets these files right (in every
run); where it does not, the rule is outside even its syntactic layer.

- `reject/lexer-division-after-radix-number` — `x = 0x10 / 1, 'a/b'`: regexContext.divisionAfterTypes lists Number and BigInt, not HexNumber, OctalNumber or BinaryNumber (a hex BigInt lexes as HexNumber).
- `reject/member-bracket-comma-expression` — `a[0, 1]`, `a?.[0, 1]`, `of[0, 1]`: MemberExpression `[ Expression ]` and OptionalChain `?. [ Expression ]`; the grammar reads one AssignmentExpression.
- `reject/decorator-private-member` — `@C.#a class D {}` inside the class body: DecoratorMemberExpression `. PrivateIdentifier`.
- `reject/await-context-leaks-into-function` — `class C { static { (function (x = await) {}) } }`: a function's FormalParameters and body are [~Await]; the parameters inherit the block's context instead.
- `reject/bigint-binding-property-key` — `let { 1n: a } = {}`: a BindingProperty's PropertyName is a LiteralPropertyName, which includes NumericLiteral (a BigInt among them); the object literal `({ 1n: a })` already parses.
- `reject/lexer-optional-chain-before-digit` — `true ?.30 : false`: OptionalChainingPunctuator is `?. [lookahead ∉ DecimalDigit]`.
- `reject/stage3-import-defer` — `import defer * as ns from "m"` and `import.defer(…)`: the grammar has neither. Decided: add to the JavaScript grammar (TypeScript follows tsc).
- `reject/stage3-source-phase-imports` — `import source x from "m"` and `import.source(…)`: the grammar has neither. Decided: add to the JavaScript grammar.
- `reject/annexb-legacy-numeric-literals` — `01`, `08`, `019` in sloppy script code: the lexer has no such token, so `010` is refused outright. Decided: accept.
- `reject/annexb-html-comments` — `<!--` and a line-leading `-->` are comments in script code only; in module code they are not comments (`a <!--b` is `a < !--b` there). Without the script / module goal, accepting them changes the meaning of valid module code.

- `accept/rest-element-shape` — `function f(...a = 1) {}`, `function f(...a,) {}`, `var [...a, b] = c`, `({...a,} = b)` in binding position: FunctionRestParameter and BindingRestElement are `... BindingIdentifier | ... BindingPattern`, last, with no Initializer and no comma after.
- `accept/declaration-in-statement-position` — `while (x) function f() {}`, `if (x) class C {}`, `for (;;) const y = 1`, `label: async function f() {}`: the body of if / while / for / with / a label is a Statement, and Statement has no Declaration (Annex B adds only the sloppy `if (x) function f() {}` and `label: function f() {}`). The grammar puts Decl in Stmt.
- `accept/import-export-not-top-level` — `{ import v from "m"; }`, `function* g() { export default null; }`: ImportDeclaration and ExportDeclaration are ModuleItems, at a module's top level only, in no goal anywhere else. The grammar puts them in Decl, which every block reaches.
- `accept/await-yield-identifier-reference` — IdentifierReference and LabelIdentifier are `[~Yield] yield` / `[~Await] await`, parameterised productions the engine has ([Await]/[Yield] families): `({await})` in an async function, `({yield})` in a generator, `yield: ;` in a generator, `await` in a class static block.
- `accept/for-in-of-initializer` — `for (let x = 1 of y)`, `for (var [a] = 1 of y)`, `for (let x = 1 in o)`, `for (x = 1 in o)`: ForInOfStatement has no initializer; Annex B (B.3.5) adds only the sloppy `for (var BindingIdentifier Initializer in Expression)`.
- `accept/numeric-literal-lexical` — `01n` (no BigInt suffix on a legacy octal), a NumericLiteralSeparator in a legacy-octal-like literal or after a leading zero: the token reads them.
- `accept/restricted-production-line-break` — `throw⏎1`, `x⏎=> 1`, `async x⏎=> 1`: the restricted productions forbid the line break, and no ASI applies.
- `accept/let-bracket-lookahead` — `for (;;) let⏎[a] = 0;`: an ExpressionStatement may not begin with `let [`, and a LexicalDeclaration is no Statement, so no production derives it.
- `accept/yield-precedence` — `yield 3 + yield 4`, `yield ? a : b`, `yield = 1` in a generator: YieldExpression is an AssignmentExpression alternative, not a UnaryExpression; the grammar lists `yield` with the prefix operators.
- `accept/using-binding-pattern` — `using x = 1, [a] = b`: a `using` LexicalBinding is a BindingIdentifier (`BindingList[~Pattern]`); only a leading `using [` is an expression (element access).
- `accept/string-line-terminator` — DoubleStringCharacter / SingleStringCharacter exclude LF and CR. `String_` is shared with JSX attribute values, which may span lines (the expected-fail in test/js-conformance.ts).
- `accept/coalesce-mixed-with-logical` — `0 && 0 ?? true`, `a ?? b || c`: CoalesceExpression's operands are BitwiseORExpressions, so neither side may be a bare `&&` / `||`.
- `accept/accessor-parameters` — `get x(a) {}`: a getter's parameter list is `( )`; a setter has exactly one PropertySetParameterList.
- `accept/in-operator-in-for-init` — `for (true ? 0 : 0 in {};;)`: the initializer is an Expression[~In] and ConditionalExpression passes ?In to both branches.
- `accept/switch-statement-outside-clause` — `switch (x) { a = 2; case 0: }`: a CaseBlock holds CaseClauses and a DefaultClause only; the grammar's SwitchCase rule has a bare Stmt arm.
- `accept/strict-mode` — Valid in sloppy mode, an error in strict code (reserved words `let` / `static` / `implements` / `yield` …, `with`, legacy octal literals and escapes, `delete x`, `eval` / `arguments` as targets or bindings, duplicate parameters, Annex B's `if (x) function f() {}`; class bodies are strict). Without a strict mode switch the grammar accepts the sloppy reading.
- `accept/module-goal` — Valid in a script, an error in module code: `await` as an identifier, module code is strict, top-level `new.target` / `super`, import / export / `import.meta` in a Script. Without the script / module goal the grammar accepts the script reading.
- `accept/return-outside-function` — ReturnStatement is a Statement[+Return] only: script top level and class static blocks are [~Return]. The engine has no [Return] parameter.
- `accept/private-names` — Early error: a `#name` declared twice, used without a declaration in an enclosing class, `#constructor`, `delete this.#x`.
- `accept/assignment-target` — Early error: AssignmentTargetType is not simple (`1 = 2`, `a?.b = 1`, `f() += 1`, `++this`), or an ObjectLiteral / ArrayLiteral on the left of `=` / in a for-in/of head does not refine to an AssignmentPattern (`[...a, b] = c`, `({a: 1} = b)`). The parser enforces the LeftHandSideExpression shape only (docs/CORRECTNESS.md).
- `accept/escaped-keyword` — Early error: an IdentifierName whose escapes spell a reserved word is neither that keyword nor an identifier (`v\u0061r x`, `\u0061sync function f() {}`, `yi\u0065ld` in a generator).
- `accept/duplicate-bindings` — Early error: LexicallyDeclaredNames with a duplicate, or one that also occurs in VarDeclaredNames (`let a; var a`, `let a; let a`, a `catch (e)` with `let e` in its block, duplicate parameters where they are not allowed).
- `accept/regexp-pattern` — Early error: the body must parse with the Pattern grammar (named groups, quantifiers, class escapes, `u` / `v` rules) and the flags must be known and unique. The token reads any body and flag run.
- `accept/super-new-target` — Early error: SuperCall outside a derived constructor, SuperProperty outside a method, `new.target` outside a function.
- `accept/use-strict-with-non-simple-parameters` — Early error: ContainsUseStrict of the body is true and IsSimpleParameterList is false.
- `accept/await-yield-binding-identifier` — Early error: BindingIdentifier derives `yield` and `await`, and "It is a Syntax Error if this production has a [Yield] / [Await] parameter". The grammar keeps them names at binding position, as tsc's parser does.
- `accept/arguments-in-class-field` — Early error: ContainsArguments of a field's Initializer.
- `accept/labels-break-continue` — Early error: an undefined or duplicate label, `continue` outside an iteration, `break` outside a breakable statement, IsLabelledFunction.
- `accept/class-element-names` — Early error: a special method (getter, setter, generator, async) or field named `constructor`, a static element named `prototype`, two constructors.
- `accept/await-yield-in-parameters` — Early error: FormalParameters Contains YieldExpression / AwaitExpression.
- `accept/declaration-without-initializer` — Early error: a LexicalBinding without an Initializer when IsConstantDeclaration (`const x;`) or IsUsingDeclaration (`using x;`).
- `accept/let-as-lexical-name` — Early error: BoundNames of a LexicalDeclaration or ForDeclaration contains "let" (`const let = 1`, `for (let let in o)`).
- `accept/optional-chain-template` — Early error: `OptionalChain :: ?. TemplateLiteral` and `OptionalChain TemplateLiteral` are productions with "It is a Syntax Error if any source text is matched by this production" (`a?.b`x``).
- `accept/using-placement` — Early error: a CaseClause / DefaultClause StatementList may not contain a UsingDeclaration or AwaitUsingDeclaration.
- `accept/static-block-contexts` — Early error: ContainsArguments / ContainsAwait of ClassStaticBlockStatementList, and `yield` / `await` reserved there by the block's own [~Yield, +Await] context.
- `accept/template-escape` — Early error: "It is a Syntax Error if the [Tagged] parameter was not set and NotEscapeSequence is matched" (`\9`, `\u{`, `\x0`).
- `accept/cover-initialized-name` — Early error: `({ a = 1 })` is matched by the cover grammar for `({ a = 1 } = b)` and is an error unless it refines to an AssignmentPattern.

## TypeScript: `typescript.ts` on the valid tests

TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript, so every test that must parse must parse with `typescript.ts` too,
unless TypeScript rejects that syntax by design: then tsc's own parser, on the file as a `.ts` file, rejects it as
well, and its diagnostic is the evidence. A file `javascript.ts` also rejects is referenced by its JavaScript
class, not classed again. A rejection tsc does not share and the JavaScript grammar does not either would be a
TypeScript grammar bug with no class yet (`ts/unknown`), and fails the gate. The negative tests are not asked of
the TypeScript grammar; there it is held to tsc's parser ([CORRECTNESS.md](CORRECTNESS.md)).

**20179 of 20200 valid tests parse (99.9%)** · by design 10 · as in JavaScript 11 · unclassified 0 · crash 0

| cell | cause | files | witness | evidence |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| `ts/by-design` | TypeScript rejects it (JavaScript class `reject/annexb-html-comments`) | 7 | `annexB/language/comments/multi-line-html-close.js` | tsc TS1109: Expression expected. |
| `ts/by-design` | TypeScript rejects it (JavaScript class `reject/annexb-html-comments`) | 1 | `annexB/language/comments/single-line-html-open.js` | tsc TS1110: Type expected. |
| `ts/by-design` | TypeScript rejects it (JavaScript class `reject/annexb-legacy-numeric-literals`) | 1 | `language/literals/numeric/legacy-octal-integer.js` | tsc TS1121: Octal literals are not allowed. Use the syntax '0o0'. |
| `ts/by-design` | TypeScript rejects it (JavaScript class `reject/annexb-legacy-numeric-literals`) | 1 | `language/literals/numeric/non-octal-decimal-integer.js` | tsc TS1489: Decimals with leading zeros are not allowed. |
| `ts/as-javascript` | the JavaScript class `reject/lexer-division-after-radix-number` | 3 | `language/expressions/division/bigint-arithmetic.js` | tsc's .ts parser accepts it |
| `ts/as-javascript` | the JavaScript class `reject/member-bracket-comma-expression` | 3 | `language/expressions/dynamic-import/assignment-expression/call-expr-expr.js` | tsc's .ts parser accepts it |
| `ts/as-javascript` | the JavaScript class `reject/decorator-private-member` | 2 | `language/expressions/class/decorator/syntax/class-valid/decorator-member-expr-private-identifier.js` | tsc's .ts parser accepts it |
| `ts/as-javascript` | the JavaScript class `reject/await-context-leaks-into-function` | 1 | `language/expressions/function/static-init-await-reference.js` | tsc's .ts parser accepts it |
| `ts/as-javascript` | the JavaScript class `reject/bigint-binding-property-key` | 1 | `language/expressions/object/literal-property-name-bigint.js` | tsc's .ts parser accepts it |

## Early errors: a checker over the tree, not the grammar: not built

The static-semantic rules ("It is a Syntax Error if …") stay out of the context-free grammar, but not out of
the project: acorn enforces all but a handful of them (the calibration below), so a JavaScript front end is
expected to. They belong to a pass over the parsed tree, which does not exist yet. This table is its
specification, ranked by the files each rule decides: **tree** means the node and its ancestors suffice; **scope**
means the pass must collect the names each scope (or class) declares.

| class | files | needs | what the checker reads |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `accept/private-names`: private names | 346 | scope | the private names each class declares, resolved through the enclosing classes (duplicates, getter / setter pairing, undeclared uses), plus `delete` of a private reference |
| `accept/assignment-target`: an invalid assignment target, or a literal that does not cover an AssignmentPattern | 322 | tree | the left side of an assignment, an update or a for-in/of head: AssignmentTargetType, and the refinement of a literal to an AssignmentPattern |
| `accept/escaped-keyword`: a keyword written with a Unicode escape | 304 | tree | an identifier token: its escape-decoded text against the reserved words, with the enclosing function kind for `await` / `yield` |
| `accept/duplicate-bindings`: duplicate or conflicting declarations | 248 | scope | the declared names of every block, function, switch and module scope: LexicallyDeclaredNames against themselves and against VarDeclaredNames, and parameter names |
| `accept/regexp-pattern`: a regular expression's pattern or flags | 170 | tree | a regular-expression token: its body against the Pattern grammar, its flags against the flag set |
| `accept/super-new-target`: `super` and `new.target` outside their contexts | 154 | tree | a `super` / `new.target` node and its enclosing function and method kinds |
| `accept/use-strict-with-non-simple-parameters`: "use strict" in a function with a non-simple parameter list | 110 | tree | a function node: its parameter list's shape and its body's directive prologue |
| `accept/await-yield-binding-identifier`: `await` / `yield` as a binding name in an async function / generator | 74 | tree | a binding name and its enclosing function kinds (async, generator, static block) |
| `accept/arguments-in-class-field`: `arguments` in a class field initializer | 58 | tree | a field initializer: does it contain `arguments` outside a non-arrow function |
| `accept/labels-break-continue`: labels, `break` and `continue` | 53 | tree | a statement and its enclosing labels and iteration / breakable statements, stopping at function and static-block boundaries |
| `accept/class-element-names`: class elements named `constructor` / `prototype` | 44 | tree | a class body: element names and kinds (`constructor`, `prototype`, a second constructor) |
| `accept/await-yield-in-parameters`: an `await` / `yield` expression in formal parameters | 20 | tree | a parameter list: does it contain a YieldExpression / AwaitExpression outside a nested function |
| `accept/declaration-without-initializer`: `const` / `using` without an initializer | 9 | tree | a `const` / `using` binding: does it have an initializer (outside a for-in/of head) |
| `accept/let-as-lexical-name`: `let` as a lexically bound name | 9 | tree | a lexical declaration's bound names: is one of them `let` |
| `accept/optional-chain-template`: a template after an optional chain | 8 | tree | an optional chain: is a template literal applied to it |
| `accept/using-placement`: a `using` declaration directly in a switch clause | 4 | tree | a `using` declaration and its parent: a case / default clause directly |
| `accept/static-block-contexts`: `arguments`, `await` and `yield` in a class static block | 3 | tree | a class static block: does it contain `arguments` or an AwaitExpression outside a nested function |
| `accept/template-escape`: a NotEscapeSequence in an untagged template | 3 | tree | an untagged template token: does it contain a NotEscapeSequence |
| `accept/cover-initialized-name`: a CoverInitializedName in an object literal | 1 | tree | an object literal not refined to an AssignmentPattern: does it contain a CoverInitializedName |

Tree alone: 1346 files; scope analysis: 594 files. The strict-mode and Module-goal rules (`needs-parameter` above) are early errors too where they forbid a name or a statement; they are counted there because they need the goal and mode first.

## Calibration: production parsers on the same files

How many test262 parse verdicts each parser gets right (read-only; no gate rides on these columns beyond
the record being current). acorn: `ecmaVersion: 'latest'`, `sourceType` per the test, strict runs with
`"use strict";` prepended, right only if right in every run. tsc: `ts.createSourceFile` as a `.js` file (a
module test forced to module detection), right only if no parse diagnostic exactly where test262 expects
none; "+ binder" also counts the binder's diagnostics (`bindSourceFile`: strict-mode words, duplicate
declarations, labels, which tsc reports outside its parser; it includes TypeScript's own checks).

| parser | right | of 24677 | on the 20200 valid tests | on the 4477 parse-negative tests |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `javascript.ts` (interpreter) | 21296 | 86.3% | 19938 (98.7%) | 1358 (30.3%) |
| acorn 8.16.0 | 24394 | 98.9% | 19926 (98.6%) | 4468 (99.8%) |
| tsc 5.9.3 parser | 21391 | 86.7% | 20123 (99.6%) | 1268 (28.3%) |
| tsc 5.9.3 parser + binder | 21829 | 88.5% | 19934 (98.7%) | 1895 (42.3%) |

Of the 3119 WE-ACCEPT files, acorn also accepts 7 (in every run), tsc's parser 2701, tsc's parser + binder 2074.
